column2: Turns an amino acid into an aldehyde with one carbon fewer. It's part of the Maillard browning chemistry behind the smell of baking bread, roasting coffee and chocolate.
Sounds deeply obscure, but its copper-catalysed version is the flagship of click chemistry, which won the 2022 Nobel Prize. Plenty of chemists will say it.
